fixes.explanation: Isaac was Abraham's son (Genesis 21:3), so I see why you picked him. But Paul names who the One is, and it isn't Isaac. He says the seed is Christ.

Right, baker. Paul says the law that came 430 years later “…does not revoke the covenant previously established by God, so as to nullify the promise.” The law arrives late, but it doesn't wipe out what came first. Just before this, Paul points out that even a human covenant, once it is ratified, cannot be canceled or amended.

Exactly, friend. Paul says, “…God freely granted it to Abraham through a promise.” He sets that against the law, saying if the inheritance depends on the law, then it no longer depends on a promise. So the promise is the word to hold onto.

That's it, friend. Paul asks if the law is opposed to the promises of God, and his answer is, “Certainly not!” Then he gives his reason: “For if a law had been given that could impart life, then righteousness would certainly have come from the law.” So the law and the promises aren't rivals.

That's not what Paul says, friend. He says, “You are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.” The law became our guardian to lead us to Christ, and then he says, “Now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian.” So sonship comes through faith, not through the guardian.

That's not in the verse, baker. Paul says you're “…heirs according to the promise.” The word works isn't there. Earlier he said that if the inheritance depends on the law, then it no longer depends on a promise (Galatians 3:18).

This one's true, friend. Paul says God sent His Son “…to redeem those under the law, that we might receive our adoption as sons.” So the redeeming has a purpose, and the purpose is adoption as sons. Then Paul says that because you are sons, God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, crying out, “Abba, Father!” (Galatians 4:6).
Paul doesn't use the word guest, friend. He says, “…you are no longer a slave, but a son; and since you are a son, you are also an heir through God.” Son and heir are the words he lands on.
Not a worker, baker. Paul says, “…you are no longer a slave, but a son…” Then he adds that since you are a son, you are also “…an heir through God.” That's the word he lands on.
